supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to the approved PixelForge updater: pfupdater.exe ran as leo.martins and connected through the proxy to updates.pixelforge-suite.com, an inventory-approved update endpoint. The observed successful connections recur at roughly five-minute intervals; one attempt was denied for missing proxy authentication.

There was a successful network logon for sam.okafor on WS-SOKAFOR-01 with WS-LMARTINS-01 recorded as the workstation and its IP as the source. This is inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01, but the logon alone does not establish what was accessed or whether it was authorized.
WS-LMARTINS-01 connected to FILE-NWD-01 over SMB; the file server recorded an ANONYMOUS LOGON for that connection. The available records do not show which share or resource was accessed.

FILE-NWD-01 subsequently made an RPC endpoint-mapper connection to WS-LMARTINS-01. This is unexplained by the available records and does not match the stated patching procedure, which uses WS-SOKAFOR-01 to run the update script.

A SYSTEM-launched DropboxUpdate.exe process ran on WS-LMARTINS-01. The host also queried x7k9m2.akamaized.net, resolving to 151.101.25.122. Dropbox is not among the approved services in the provided inventory, but these records do not show Dropbox file-sync activity or prove the process was malicious.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show CONNECT tunnels, not the HTTPS contents; for example, the PixelForge connections are identified by destination and process correlation, not by inspected application payload (T046-00101, T046-00103, T046-00104).

The available file-server evidence records SMB and RPC connections but does not identify the accessed share contents, the RPC operation, or a command executed on WS-LMARTINS-01 (T046-00008, T046-00011, T046-00015, T046-00067, T046-00069).
The Dropbox-related records show updater execution and a DNS query, but no corresponding proxy connection or evidence of file uploads or downloads (T046-00119, T046-00124, T046-00126).
claims_not_established: The records do not establish whether sam.okafor's successful network logon from WS-LMARTINS-01 was authorized or used to perform administrative actions (T046-00023, T046-00024).

The records do not establish that the SMB or RPC activity involved remote execution, data access beyond the observed connection, or malicious lateral movement (T046-00008, T046-00011, T046-00015, T046-00067, T046-00069).
The records do not establish that DropboxUpdate.exe performed file sharing, exfiltrated data, or was a malicious or tampered binary (T046-00119, T046-00124, T046-00126).

The records do not show whether the PixelForge update content was authentic or what it contained, despite the process and destination matching the approved updater activity (T046-00101, T046-00103, T046-00104).
additional_evidence_needed: Verify with sam.okafor and WS-SOKAFOR-01 authentication/audit logs whether the network logon from WS-LMARTINS-01 was expected; review any resulting administrative activity.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 SMB share-access and process/command logs, plus WS-LMARTINS-01 RPC and remote-service/task creation evidence, to determine what the connections did.
Verify the DropboxUpdate.exe signature, installation provenance, persistence configuration, and any associated file-sync or proxy activity against the organization's software policy.
Obtain proxy TLS inspection or endpoint application telemetry for the PixelForge connections if validating update content or payload authenticity is required.
